source.extractionNote: Two sets on the page: Message Input (10 variants) and Attachment (2), each with its own metadata frame. Two loose Message Input instances on the page are ignored.

summary: A composer for conversational, AI-assisted surfaces: type, attach, dictate, record a voice message, hear the reply.

intent.empty: The resting composer, nothing typed. Send stays off until there is something to send.
intent.filled: A typed message ready to go. Send turns on here and nowhere earlier.
intent.attachment-open: The attachment tray is showing its choices. Transient, not a resting state.
intent.listening: Dictation is capturing speech. Extra tools drop away so nothing competes with Stop.
intent.transcribing: Speech captured, text not back yet. Everything is off, so it must not linger.
intent.dictated: Dictation returned text the person can still edit. Treat it as filled, not as sent.
intent.recording: A voice message is being captured. Unlike listening, this ends as audio.
intent.playback: A take waiting to be sent or discarded. The only chance to hear it first.
intent.speaking: The assistant is replying aloud. The only state with no toolbar at all.
intent.disabled: Composing is unavailable. Say why in the value text, or there is nothing to act on.

attachmentFileSlot.intent: Holds whatever the product attaches, above the text. Empty until the product fills it.

moreToolsSlot.intent: Room for product tools beside Attachment. Icon controls only, at the toolbar's size.

subcomponents.name: Attachment
subcomponents.summary: The attachment control in Message Input's toolbar. Closed it is a single add button. Open it expands into a row of attachment type controls the product supplies through a slot.

intent.false: The resting control, one button. Use it wherever the choices are not needed on screen.
intent.true: The tray is showing its choices. Transient, because the toolbar loses its other tools while it is open.

attachmentControlSlot.intent: The attachment types the product offers. Left empty it opens onto nothing.

anatomy.sample: four Icon Buttons, Flavour=subtle: attachment, camera, sticker, audio

states.What changes: The glyph becomes close, the button takes its pressed surface and the slot appears.

behavior.Description: No transition is defined. Opening is a swap, not an animation.
Open, it takes the room the More Tools slot would use, and the parent drops that slot.

content.Description: Takes one icon control per attachment type. Four fit at the drawn width.
Drawn by the component. Its glyph flips between add and close with Open.

do: Fill the slot with the types the product supports. An open tray with nothing in it is a dead end.
Close the tray once a type is chosen. It costs the toolbar its other tools while open.
dont: Don't leave it open as a resting state. The More Tools slot disappears while it is.
Don't put labelled buttons in the slot. It is sized for icon controls at the toolbar's height.

accessibility: The toggle is an icon with no text. It needs a name, and the name changes with Open.
Opening the tray reveals controls without moving focus. That change has to be announced.
Each control in the slot is an icon only, so every one needs a name saying what it attaches.
The tray and the toolbar share a row. Keyboard order has to follow what a person sees.

layoutTheming.Description: A 36 Icon Button at Shape=full, Flavour=subtle.
156 by 36 when open, sized for four 36 controls.
The toggle takes interactive/ghost/background, default closed and pressed open.

tokens.glyphNote: All icons are font glyphs in the rounded family and take currentColor from their Icon Button or Assist Chip. All exist in packages/icons/codepoints.json and none is retired.
tokens.themeAxes: palette (Light, Dark, AAA Light, AAA Dark), size (Desktop, Mobile, Tablet, Desktop Compact) and every brand extension.

states.What changes: The value moves to foreground/primary and Send enables.
Attachment expands to its open form and the More Tools slot drops out.
Text swaps for the Voice bar. Actions become Stop and a disabled Send.
The Voice bar holds while every control disables.
The Voice bar swaps back to Text carrying the transcript, and Send enables.
The Voice bar gains a foreground/error dot and a discard control. Send stays off.
The Voice bar gains Play, a full waveform and an elapsed timer. Send enables.
The body becomes an orb and a caption. The toolbar is gone entirely.
Surface and border take their disabled tokens and every control turns off.

behavior.Description: No transition is defined. Each state is a swap of the body region and the toolbar.
Text, Voice and Speaking are mutually exclusive. Only one is ever present.
Send is on only where there is something to send, at filled, attachment-open, dictated and playback.
Dictation ends as editable text. Recording ends as an audio message. They share the Voice bar and nothing else.

content.Description: The typed or dictated text. Not exposed as an input, so it comes from the implementation.
The only places a product adds content of its own.
Sits above the text on filled and attachment-open.
Sits beside Attachment in the toolbar. Absent on attachment-open and listening.
Every control is an Icon Button at Shape=full. Attachment has its own frame.
The waveform, timer, orb and caption are drawn by the component, not passed in.

do: Say why in the value text when disabled. A composer that refuses input without a reason reads as broken.
Keep playback in the recording flow. It is the only chance to hear a take before sending it.
dont: Don't use listening for a voice message. It ends as text, recording ends as audio.
Don't put a toolbar back during speaking. It is absent so nothing can be composed over the reply.

accessibility: State changes are not announced. Dictation starting, transcription finishing and the assistant speaking all need announcing by the surrounding structure.
The waveform and the orb carry no text. The label and timer beside them are all a reader gets, so they have to say what is happening.
Send is disabled in five of the ten states. Disabled does not say why, so the value text or a nearby message has to.
Every control is an icon with no label. Each needs a name, and the names differ by state even where the glyph repeats.
While speaking there is no toolbar and only Stop speaking interrupts it. That control has to be reachable by keyboard.

accessibleNames._note: Taken from the layer names in Figma.

layoutTheming.Description: 440 wide. Height follows the body region, 130 empty, 146 voice, 168 with an attachment row and 276 speaking.
space/md on all four sides, space/sm between the body region and the toolbar.
surface/card with a border/default outline, moving to interactive/neutral/background/disabled and border/disabled when disabled.
Text, Voice or Speaking. Text carries body/medium at 16px.
Tools on the left, Actions on the right. Controls are 36 square, Send and Stop 40.
48 tall on surface/track, holding a 2px bar waveform, a label, a timer and one trailing control.

visualReference.policy: No images are stored; every node deep-links into Figma so a shot can be pulled on demand and is never stale.

issues.detail: Metadata says Send and Stop are 40. Every action is an Icon Button at Size=small, bound to control/sm like the other controls.
Metadata says the Voice bar sits on surface/track. It is bound to surface/subtle.
Metadata gives heights of 130, 146, 168 and 276. The variants measure 126, 142, 164 and 272.
Metadata says every control disables. Attachment, the More Tools slot and Cancel transcription stay enabled.
Metadata says every control turns off. Attachment stays enabled, because it has no disabled option.
The Dictated chip sits in a plain frame named Attachment Slot, not in the Attachment File Slot. The metadata doesn't mention the chip.
The caption's first run is foreground/disabled and the rest foreground/primary. The metadata doesn't say what the split means.
The Attachment toggle and its slot controls are all named Icon Button, so they give no name to carry into code.
The orb rings' stroke width and opacity have no token. The Text region's minimum height has no token either.
Disabled Dictate switches Flavour from subtle to text, unlike Send, which keeps its flavour.
Dictate is dropped from Actions, leaving Send alone. The metadata doesn't say so.
Each voice state has a hint line in body/xsmall at foreground/secondary. The metadata doesn't mention it.
Four of the six rings are hidden. No motion is defined, so any animation of the orb or waveform is the implementer's call.
The recording dot is sized with space/sm and the waveform bars with stroke/thick.
The value text is not a Figma property. The metadata says it comes from the implementation.
No transition is defined for Message Input or Attachment. Each state is a swap.
